verified_checks.finding: RS's matrix device is NOT a field on a Riccati variable. It has two parts. (a) The cumulative mass matrix A(x) = int_{-inf}^x Q (Q = UU^T in Sec. 1, rank one at each x; Q = density matrix of a Hilbert-space-valued family, any rank, in v2 Sec. 2), with A' = Q, A(-inf) = 0, A(+inf) = I, 0 <= A <= I. It is explicit (no ODE, no path existence) and K-free. (b) A midpoint Schur-multiplier (double-operator) lift of a FIXED scalar function q = b_alpha = -alpha tan(alpha(s - 1/2)) on the spectrum of A, applied to the density: B_RS = sum c_rl A^r Q A^l, i.e. (B_RS)_ij = q((lambda_i + lambda_j)/2) Q_ij in A's eigenbasis. This gives the flux F_q = (1/4) sum |Q_ij|^2 q(s_ij) = (1/4) Tr(B_RS Q), the completed square ||W' - (1/2) B_RS W||_HS^2, and a pointwise positivity condition G_{q,kappa}(P, lambda) >= 0 built from q(s)q(t) + q[s,t] <= -kappa (eq. 1.4). Positivity is verified by the Stein-type identity C - TCT = DPD and a fourth-power (Schoenberg-type) embedding (Lemma 6). The sharp constant comes from kappa = alpha^2 -> pi^2 in this pointwise inequality, with the boundary flux vanishing at +-inf. COMPARISON with M_delta. Shared: both complete a square with a matrix log-derivative multiplier (262: 2a'^T B a <= |a'|^2 + a^T B^2 a; RS: ||W' - B_RS W/2||^2). Both reduce for N = 1 to the Benguria-Loss/Keller scalar calibration, where b <-> cumulative mass is an explicit change of variables. Different: (1) direction. In RS the log-derivative matrix is an explicit LINEAR function of the density Q given A. In 262, B is a free path variable solved for by eps B' = M(B) - aa^T between endpoints K and -K (existence by mod-2 degree), and the density is a NONLINEAR function of B through the constraint M(B) = aa^T. (2) RS has no energy scales K, no sigma, no pencil K^2 - 2sB + s^2, no phase-space s-integral, no regularization delta and no trace primitive J (F_q is a flux, not a gradient potential); it relies on gamma = 1 homogeneity (tau >= (kappa/4) Tr Q^3). (3) RS proves full-rank pointwise positivity G >= 0, whereas 262 proves a rank-one comparison. (4) The constant comes from pointwise kappa in RS and from the boundary difference J(-K) - J(K) in 262. At sigma = 1/2, M_delta = c int (log(X_s(B)+delta) - log(s^2+delta)) ds, which equals (K^2-B^2+delta)^{1/2} - delta^{1/2} on commuting data. It is K-dependent and nonlinear in B, so it is not B_RS under any reparametrization B <-> (A, Q). VERDICT: genuinely different device for the same job (a noncommutative lift of the scalar Benguria-Loss/Keller calibration); neither equivalent nor a close variant. Laptev-Weidl is cited ONLY for dimension lifting in Thm 2 and for the sharp gamma = 3/2 bound, and DLL08 only for operator-valued duality. RS uses no phase-space or Weyl-density matrix device, so that downgrade risk is not raised by RS. Corrections to the earlier snippet-level record: the phrase 'matrix correction to the kinetic energy' does not occur in RS; it is 262-S's own paraphrase (S introduction.tex:110). In v1 and v2 Sec. 1, A' = UU^T is rank one; rank > 1 occurs only in v2 Sec. 2 (Q). v1 has no operator-valued result; Prop. 4, Thm 2, Lemmas 5-6 and the co-author M.R. Schulz arrive in v2.

precedent_checks.method_as_reported: VERIFIED 2026-10-12. The proof reduces by duality to the kinetic form sum int (u_j')^2 >= (pi^2/4) int rho^3 and starts from the Sz.-Nagy scalar case. It rewrites Benguria-Loss with an auxiliary q, q' + q^2 <= -kappa, and q = b_alpha = -alpha tan(alpha(s - 1/2)), b' + b^2 = -alpha^2. Matrix extension: the cumulative mass matrix A(x) = int Q (Q = UU^T, rank one, in Sec. 1; any-rank density matrix of a Hilbert-space-valued family in v2 Sec. 2). On top of A, a midpoint Schur-multiplier lift B = sum c_rl A^r Q A^l, i.e. B_ij = q((lambda_i+lambda_j)/2) Q_ij in A's eigenbasis, gives the flux F_q = (1/4) sum |Q_ij|^2 q(s_ij) and the completed square ||W' - BW/2||^2. Positivity comes from the divided-difference condition q(s)q(t) + q[s,t] <= -kappa (eq. 1.4), verified via C - TCT = DPD and a fourth-power embedding (Lemma 6). The phrase 'matrix correction to the kinetic energy' is 262-S's paraphrase, not RS's wording. No Laptev-Weidl or phase-space matrix device: LW00 is used only for dimension lifting (Thm 2).

In 262, B is a free matrix Riccati variable with endpoints K and -K, solved for by eps B' = M(B) - aa^T. The density is the nonlinear field M(B), built from the phase-space pencil integral of f(K^2 - 2sB + s^2), and the constant comes from the boundary difference of the trace primitive J. At sigma = 1/2 the 262 field is the log-pencil integral, equal to (K^2-B^2+delta)^{1/2} - delta^{1/2} on commuting data. It is K-dependent, so it is NOT the gamma = 1 member of RS's construction under any reparametrization. RS has no energy scales, no pencil, no s-integral, no gradient primitive and no rank-one comparison.

candidates.name: Regularized energy-dependent matrix field M_delta(B) with primitive J and rank-one comparison
paper_items: I07/I08/I09 (J, mu, directional Jensen, diagonal rule, boundary values)
candidates.statement: For K = diag(k_i) > 0, delta > 0, f(0)=0, f'(y) = (y_+ + delta)^{sigma-3/2}: M(B) = c lim_R int_{-R}^{R} (f(K^2 - 2sB + s^2) - f(s^2) I) ds on Sym_N. It is a trace gradient (dJ = -tr(M dB)), equals (K^2-B^2+delta)^sigma - delta^sigma on commuting data, and M(B) = aa^T implies a^T(K^2-B^2)a >= |a|^{2q}.
candidates.interpretation: The s-integral is a phase-space (momentum) integral: X_s(B) = (s-B)^2 + (K^2-B^2) is the Fourier symbol of the constant-coefficient operator -(d/dx - iB)^2 + K^2 - B^2 (262-M trace.tex makes this explicit with nabla = d/dx - iB). Up to regularization, M(B) is the diagonal kernel of (H_B+delta)^beta/beta minus its free counterpart, i.e. a local Weyl density of a constant non-abelian 'magnetic' operator, with B the matrix Riccati variable acting as a gauge shift. In the commuting case the shift integrates out (eq:shift), giving the scalar calibration (k^2-b^2)^sigma; in the noncommuting case the shift is what makes the field affine in B and hence a gradient.

final.justification: Read-Schulz does not contain it (VERIFIED against the full v1 and v2 text on 2026-10-12). RS's matrix device is the explicit cumulative mass A(x) with a midpoint Schur-multiplier lift of a fixed scalar tangent function applied to the density. It is K-free, linear in the density, a flux rather than a gradient potential, and gives the constant through pointwise positivity. 262's field lives on the free Riccati variable B with energy scales K. It is a gradient of the trace primitive J, and its sigma=1/2 member is a log-pencil integral, not a function of (A, Q). RS also uses no Laptev-Weidl or phase-space matrix device (LW00 only for dimension lifting). RS is AI-assisted (GPT-6 Astra first version; Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 for v2), which affects the provenance flag but not the content comparison. Confidence rises from 0.40 to 0.45 because the 'sigma=1/2 member equals RS' route is closed. It rises only slightly because RS shows that a noncommutative lift of the same scalar calibration already existed at gamma = 1, so C1's claim is the specific K-dependent pencil/phase-space gradient field with its rank-one comparison, not matrix lifting per se. The grade remains borderline N2 because every ingredient is in L (scalar calibration, LT phase-space integral, trace-gradient calculus, Benguria-Loss calibration template). An expert may see M_delta as 'just' the local Weyl density of -(d/dx - iB)^2 + K^2 - B^2, a known kind of object with a gauge shift, and so a close variant of Laptev-Weidl phase-space lifting. That risk is untouched by the RS check. The rank-one comparison (I14) is proved with N2 gadgets (C4) and counts here only jointly with the field. Lean-backed: eligible for the Lean shortlist. Not a confirmed eureka step: no downstream speedup test yet.
